summary: Kernel covers kernel extensions (kexts), the IOKit base classes for in-kernel drivers, and BSD/Mach kernel interfaces. These are specific to Apple's XNU kernel and kext loading model. BifrOSt runs on Linux, where drivers are in-tree or loaded by the Linux kernel itself, and BifrOSt ships no kernel extension or kernel-resident API for apps.

features.apple: Implementing drivers, system extensions, and kexts; Installing a Custom Kernel Extension
features.note: Apple kext loading does not exist on Linux; BifrOSt has no kext installer

features.apple: Debugging a Custom Kernel Extension; Generating a Non-Maskable Interrupt
features.note: Two-Mac kernel debugging is an Apple workflow; no counterpart in BifrOSt

features.apple: IOKit Fundamentals, Hardware Families, Driver Support, IOService, IOCatalogue
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/device_registry.rs (devices, Matching, changes, DeviceWatch); springboard/src/bare/kms.rs (DRM card probing), springboard/src/media/v4l2.rs
features.note: Apps list the devices of a class with their sysfs properties, match them and see arrivals and removals by polling, with tests. There is no driver model, and drivers stay in the system.

features.apple: kern, sys, vfs, vm, net, mach, mach-o
features.bifrost: Linux kernel via libc calls (for example springboard/src/bare/bluetooth.rs uses AF_BLUETOOTH sockets)
features.note: Apple's XNU interfaces are not a public surface on Linux; apps use the Linux kernel through libc
Specific to IOKit's kernel service registry
Nothing to map; BifrOSt has no equivalent of Apple's deprecation list

gaps: No SDK API for app code to talk to a driver or read device state from the kernel; hardware access sits in the shell and daemons (springboard/src/bare/).
No kernel-level debugging workflow comparable to Apple's kext debugging (not needed for an app SDK, recorded for completeness).
